defined_by: AI Aesthetics Clinical Team + Dr. Aakriti Mehra Constraints

do_not_break: Keep session_intake_raw / session_machines_raw / skin_ai_raw as top-level containers alongside iv_scoring_output

constraints_binding.note: This engine NEVER overrides constraints. It generates candidate protocols, calls constraints.evaluate() per candidate, applies returned caps/restrictions/patches, and emits only allowed protocols.

ingredient_menu_binding.generation_rule: The model MUST ONLY propose ingredients whose canonical names exist in the constraints allowlist. Unknown ingredient => must not be proposed.
ingredient_menu_binding.naming_rule: Ingredient names must match the allowlist by exact string.

ingredient_role_semantics.purpose: Define how ingredient-list labels influence, but do not rigidly determine, protocol role assignment.

label_definitions.Base: Carrier/base fluid only. Base ingredients are not active hero/supportive ingredients and do not count toward hero/supportive logic.
label_definitions.Hero: Commonly suitable as a lead active ingredient when it strongly matches the dominant burden pattern or primary goal.
label_definitions.Supportive: Usually additive rather than lead. Best used to improve secondary-axis coverage, synergy, tolerability, hydration feel, calm/recovery quality, or protocol depth.
label_definitions.Flexible: May serve either as a hero or as a supportive depending on burden pattern, same-session objective, protocol strength needs, and additive value.

role_assignment_rules: Ingredient-list labels are semantic guidance, not hard locks.
Final protocol role is determined at protocol-construction time, not by label alone.
A Flexible ingredient may be assigned either to hero_ingredients or to supportive ingredients.
A Hero-labeled ingredient is commonly lead, but may still be used as supportive if that creates a stronger or more elegant protocol.
A Supportive-labeled ingredient should usually remain supportive unless explicitly justified by the burden pattern and protocol objective.
A Base-labeled ingredient must not be treated as a hero or supportive active.
priority_principle: Protocol role assignment must follow same-session clinical value, not rigid label literalism.
If an ingredient is better used as supportive for protocol depth and additive coverage, do not force it into hero_ingredients merely because it is Hero-labeled.
If an ingredient is Flexible and clearly central to the protocol's corrective value, it may be promoted to hero_ingredients.

helpers.any_ingredient_named: return any(ing.name == target for all bags/ingredients)

ingredients.name: canonical ingredient string (must match constraints allowlist)

budget_candidate_optional.budget_rule: If true => hero_ingredients MUST have exactly 1 item and MUST NOT be NAD+

hard_rules: All protocols MUST have hero_ingredients length between 1 and 3 (inclusive).
Budget option protocol MUST have exactly 1 hero ingredient.
Budget option MUST NOT contain NAD+ anywhere (including supporting ingredients).
If one of Option 1/2 contains NAD+, the other MUST NOT contain NAD+.
hero_selection_guidance: Hero ingredients are the 1–3 most important actives driving the main benefit today.
Carrier fluid (NS/LR) does NOT need to be a hero unless you intentionally want it as a hero.
Supporting ingredients are allowed as long as constraints allow and hero cap is respected.

supportive_policy.nad_exception: If protocol contains NAD+ anywhere, keep it standalone unless constraints explicitly allow additives.
supportive_policy.gentle_intensity_relaxation: If desired_intensity is Gentle AND safety fields are sparse/unknown, allow 0-1 supportives and prefer the lower-complexity safe build.
supportive_policy.strong_intensity_expectation: If desired_intensity is Strong and the case has >=2 meaningful burden axes, do not stop at a single-supportive build unless extra additives are redundant, blocked, or weakly additive.
quality_bar: Supportives do not count toward hero cap.
Supportives must map to (top_axes coverage OR tolerability OR synergy OR protocol depth).
Each supportive must have a clear purpose.
For non-NAD single-session options, supportives should collectively make the protocol feel materially stronger, not merely satisfy a minimum rule.
Prefer multiple non-redundant supportives when they improve same-session felt benefit and overall protocol strength.
anti_thin_protocol_rule: A non-NAD premium single-session option is weak by default if it contains only 1 hero and 1 supportive while 2 or more meaningful axes remain insufficiently covered.
If the case is mixed (e.g. hydration/recovery + oxidative + metabolic or ANS burden), the engine should try a richer layered build before accepting a thin protocol.

single_session_and_plan.format: benefits provided by the IV treatment_Hero Ingredients

treatment_synthesis_policy.core_principle: Compose protocols freely within the ingredient allowlist and constraints. Optimize for patient-perceived benefit + goal alignment + reduction of the top IV burden axes. Never exceed max 3 hero ingredients.
must_follow_rules: Only use ingredients from constraints allowlist.
Always call constraints.evaluate(candidate_protocol, full_upstream_payload) before emitting any option.
If constraints returns patched_protocol_optional, use that patched protocol in the final output.
Never propose more than 3 hero ingredients in any protocol.
Single-session Option 1 and Option 2 must be different protocols.
If one of Option 1/2 contains NAD+, the other MUST NOT contain NAD+.
Budget option must have exactly one hero ingredient and MUST NOT contain NAD+ anywhere.
If NAD+ is used: it must be standalone session; NS carrier only; slow-only; spacing rules enforced by constraints.

All non-NAD+ protocols MUST include at least 1 supportive ingredient (not counting carrier fluid) unless constraints prevent; supportives must be justified by (top_axes coverage OR tolerability OR synergy).
degrees_of_freedom: choose carrier (Normal Saline vs Lactated Ringer's)
assign doses and units (constraints may cap/patch)
assign rate_profile and min_duration (constraints may restrict/patch)
choose 1-bag vs 2-bag session IF constraints allow (default prefer 1 bag)
choose which 1–3 actives are heroes (max 3) and label others as supporting
soft_preferences: Prefer fewer total ingredients when intensity preference is Gentle or when many safety fields are unknown.
Prefer hydration + electrolyte comfort when PCCS/ASLS are high (aligns with same-day feel).
Prefer antioxidant support when ODS/DGS are high AND constraints allow (aligns with 7–14 day visible improvement).
Prefer metabolic cofactors when MONS is high (aligns with fatigue/energy).
Avoid complex multi-bag sessions unless dominant burden is very high and constraints allow.

illustrative_high_efficacy_multi_axis_pa.purpose: These examples are illustrative only and are NOT fixed recipes, templates, or constraints. They exist to signal that clinically justified complexity is acceptable and encouraged when supported by burden axes and safety constraints.
illustrative_high_efficacy_multi_axis_pa.general_principle: The presence of multiple supporting ingredients is not considered over-treatment if each ingredient is justified by a distinct physiological burden axis and constraints permit safe administration.

examples.context: High MONS with concurrent PCCS and moderate ODS; client reports fatigue with poor recovery and wants both same-day energy and near-term improvement.
examples.clinical_reasoning: It is clinically reasonable to combine metabolic cofactors, hydration/electrolyte support, and antioxidant support in a single session when each addresses a different axis and no contraindications exist.
examples.important_note: Multiple supporting ingredients may be appropriate here if they map to distinct axes rather than duplicating the same pathway.

examples.context: ASLS and PCCS are dominant with secondary MONS elevation; client has stress symptoms, poor sleep, and intermittent fatigue.
examples.clinical_reasoning: ANS-calming and hydration strategies may be prioritized while still layering light metabolic support in the same session if safety allows, rather than separating into multiple visits.
examples.important_note: Layering across axes in one session is acceptable when the goal is global autonomic and recovery improvement.

examples.context: ODS and DGS are high with moderate MSGS; client’s primary goal is glow and detox but reports low systemic energy.
examples.clinical_reasoning: Antioxidant-focused protocols may still include metabolic or electrolyte support when systemic fatigue or recovery burden is present, even if glow is the primary intent.
examples.important_note: Secondary axes should be meaningfully addressed, not tokenized, when clinically relevant.

explicit_non_constraints: These examples do NOT define ideal ingredient counts.
These examples do NOT imply required ingredient combinations.
These examples do NOT override constraints, safety checks, or hero caps.
Ingredient selection, dosing, and rates remain fully governed by constraints and clinical logic.

protocol_power_validator.purpose: Prevent thin, tidy, underpowered premium protocols from winning when a stronger layered build is clinically superior.
rules: Before finalizing Option 1 and Option 2, ask whether the protocol feels clinically meaningful for the actual same-session burden pattern.
Reject protocols that merely match the dominant axis but leave relevant secondary burdens weakly addressed.
Reject protocols that look neat but feel too thin for a Strong-intensity mixed-burden case.
If a richer non-redundant protocol is safe and meaningfully stronger, it should outrank a simpler thinner protocol.
thin_protocol_flags: 1 hero + 1 supportive in a mixed-burden strong-intensity case
dominant axis covered but #2/#3 axes only tokenized
same-day felt benefit likely weaker than a richer safe build
protocol reads like generic metabolic or antioxidant support rather than a targeted session

ingredient_building_blocks.note: Planning guide only. Not a fixed protocol menu. Ingredient names listed here are examples that MUST exist in the constraints allowlist; if your allowlist differs, remove or update.

composition_guidance: Generate a clean candidate focused tightly on the dominant axis and primary goal.
This candidate may remain relatively simple, but must still include meaningful supportives if non-NAD.
Use this as one candidate family, not as the default winner.

candidate_design_templates.when: top_axes has 2 or 3 meaningful burdens OR desired_intensity is Strong
composition_guidance: Generate a layered candidate that addresses the dominant axis plus at least one secondary axis in the SAME session.
Prioritize additive felt benefit and stronger same-session effect.
Do not force minimalism if extra ingredients are justified and non-redundant.
Prefer elegant layering over sparse neatness.

candidate_design_templates.when: ASLS or PCCS or FENS is among top_axes OR recent stressors/sleep debt/recovery burden are present
composition_guidance: Generate a candidate optimized for same-day felt improvement: hydration feel, calm/ANS, recovery comfort, less drained feeling, better reset quality.
Layer supportives if they materially improve same-session experience.

candidate_design_templates.when: ODS or MSGS or ILS is among top_axes
composition_guidance: Generate a candidate that meaningfully combines antioxidant / metabolic repair logic when clinically justified.
Do not reduce this family to a single antioxidant plus token metabolic support if multiple burdens are relevant.

candidate_design_templates.when: MONS is among top_axes OR primary_goal indicates Energy/Focus/Performance
composition_guidance: Generate a candidate centered on energy and output, but still address hydration/ANS burden if relevant.
Avoid making B-complex-only style builds the automatic answer.

candidate_design_templates.when: NAD+ seems strongly ideal (MONS very high AND constraints likely allow AND desired_intensity not Gentle)
candidate_design_templates.note: Do not force NAD+. Only include when it genuinely wins on objectives.

generation_steps: 1) Compute top_axes: top 2-3 axes by highest scores from iv_scoring_output.scores_public_0_100.
2) Generate diverse candidates using the templates above, varying carrier/bag size/ingredient sets/doses/rate_profile.
3) For each candidate: ensure every ingredient name is in constraints allowlist; otherwise rebuild candidate.
4) For each candidate: assign hero_ingredients (1–3) and ensure hero_count<=3. If >3, rebuild or reduce heroes.
6) Discard blocked candidates. Keep allowed and allowed_with_cautions. Keep doctor_approval_required but rank lower for consumer options.

7) If constraints returns patched_protocol_optional, replace candidate with patched protocol and re-check hero_count<=3; if patch breaks hero cap, adjust heroes (not ingredients) to max 3 while keeping protocol unchanged.

8) Rank candidates using qualitative scoring: dominant-axis correction strength + secondary-axis coverage + goal alignment + intensity match + same-day perceived benefit + protocol coherence + additive layering quality + elegance. Simplicity may help only when extra ingredients are redundant, weakly additive, or poorly tolerated.

9) If insufficient allowed candidates, iterate by simplifying only where complexity is redundant or blocked. Do not automatically collapse to fewer ingredients if a richer build is still safe, coherent, and meaningfully stronger.
selection_rules_for_top2: Option 2 = next best ranked candidate different from Option 1.
NAD mutual exclusion: if Option 1 contains NAD+, Option 2 must NOT contain NAD+; if Option 1 does not contain NAD+, Option 2 may contain NAD+ only if it is the best remaining and constraints allow.

hard_rules: Budget option MUST NOT contain NAD+ anywhere
Budget option MUST have exactly 1 hero ingredient
Budget option should be as simple as possible while still beneficial
generation_steps: 2) Propose a minimal protocol using 1 hero ingredient aligned to dominant_axis; choose carrier and bag size conservatively.
3) Ensure NAD+ is not used anywhere.
4) Run constraints.evaluate(). If blocked, switch hero ingredient and retry.
5) Validate: hero_ingredients length==1 AND hero != 'NAD+' AND protocol does not contain NAD+ anywhere. If violated, rebuild.

plan_option_3_to_4_months.principle: Adaptive plan: each session is generated on the day using the same synthesis loop, guided by phase objectives, then constraints-validated.

phase_objectives: Target persistent top axes after phase 1
Introduce more axis-specific actives if constraints allow
Balance same-day feel with 7–14 day improvement

nad_handling.note: NAD+ may appear only as a standalone session, only if optimal in that week and constraints allow. Budget option never includes NAD+.

sessions.note: Each later session is re-generated on its day using updated inputs and re-validated by constraints.

steps: 1) Assert required top-level keys exist per integration_contract.
3) Rank axes by descending score; derive dominant_axis and top_axes (top 2-3).
4) Generate single-session candidates using candidate_generation_loop.single_session (free composition within allowlist).
5) Constraints-evaluate each candidate; apply patched_protocol_optional when present; enforce hero cap (<=3 heroes).
6) Select Option 1 and Option 2 per selection rules (including NAD mutual exclusion).
7) Generate Budget option using candidate_generation_loop.budget_option; constraints-evaluate; enforce budget rules (1 hero, no NAD+ anywhere).

8) Generate full 14-week plan. For EACH week: Run candidate_generation_loop.single_session, Apply phase objectives, Call constraints.evaluate(), Enforce hero cap and supportive coverage audit, Attach recommended_protocol for that week

8A) For plan_option: MUST generate sessions[] with >= 6 sessions, Each session must contain a newly generated protocol, Each session must pass constraints.evaluate(), MUST NOT reuse same protocol across all sessions
10) Emit only allowed/allowed_with_cautions options; if doctor_approval_required, mark clearly and include constraint messages.

notes: Generative planner: composes protocols freely inside constraints + ingredient menu.
Max 3 hero ingredients in any protocol.
Option 1 and 2 are top-2 single-session choices; NAD+ is not preferred but can win if truly ideal.
If one of Option 1/2 contains NAD+, the other must not contain NAD+.
Budget option: exactly 1 hero ingredient and never NAD+ anywhere.
After client selection, execution engine generates step-by-step nurse/therapist run sheet.

identity_and_consent: Confirm patient name + DOB (or clinic ID).
Confirm consent for IV session and selected option.

during_infusion: BP/HR trend check at least every 15 min or sooner if symptomatic

must_record: all additives and final doses actually administered
start time, end time, total duration
rate profile used and any rate changes

treatment_execution_engine.trigger: After client selects one option, generate nurse/therapist step-by-step instructions for the chosen protocol.

how_to_build_run_sheet: 1) Find the chosen protocol in treatment_generation_output by selected_protocol_id.
2) Re-run constraints.evaluate(chosen_protocol, full_upstream_payload) with today's vitals (recommended).
3) If constraints returns patched_protocol_optional, use that protocol for execution steps.
4) Build preflight checks from clinic_sop_defaults + constraints actions (hard blocks / doctor approval).
5) Build setup and administration steps from protocol bags/ingredients + any constraints restrictions (dose caps, slow-only, min duration).
6) Monitoring plan: use clinic_sop_defaults.monitoring_defaults; if protocol contains NAD+ => apply nad_specific_frequency_override.
